about: Evidence recommendations for the national security policies of Annex F of the UAE Information Assurance Standard v2.1, as extra rows of the UAE IA library (rows F1-*, F2-*, F3-* and F4-* of uae_ia_annex_f_rows.json): F1 National Encryption Policy (Table 13), F2 National Secure Remote Work Policy (Table 14), F3 National Third Party Security Policy (Table 15) and F4 National Data Exchange Security Policy (Table 16). Authored for this library: the annex names no evidence. Every item is grounded in the row's own Objective and asks for what an assessor of that policy section would want to see beyond what the UAE IA v2.1 controls the row maps to already ask for; the annex has one Objective per row, so the items carry no 'covers'. build_uae_ia_annex_f_rows.py merges this file into the generated rows as evidence_requirements {name, description, filetype}; collection_frequency is kept where the item is event-driven or continuous (the seeder reads it from dict entries and otherwise defaults to annually).

F1-2.1.name: National encryption conformance review
F1-2.1.description: Review comparing the entity's cryptographic standards and practices with each section of the national encryption requirements, listing the gaps found with their owners and target dates.

F1-2.1.name: Approved cryptographic algorithms and key lengths
F1-2.1.description: Standard listing the algorithms, modes and key lengths approved for each use, such as storage, transmission and hashing, and those prohibited, with its owner, version and approval date.

F1-2.2.name: Encryption risk assessment
F1-2.2.description: Assessment of the security and privacy risks that arise where data is not encrypted or only weakly encrypted, with the rating, owner and treatment chosen for each risk.

F1-2.2.name: Encryption risk remediation tracker
F1-2.2.description: Tracker of the actions that remove the encryption weaknesses found, with the owner, the due date and the completion date of each, so the time taken to fix them can be seen.

F1-2.3.name: Encryption legal and regulatory requirements map
F1-2.3.description: Map of each law, regulation or standard that applies to the entity's use of encryption to the feature of the cryptographic solution that meets it, with the owner and the date last checked.

F1-2.4.name: Encryption requirements by classification level
F1-2.4.description: Table that states, for each classification level, the encryption the entity applies to data at rest and in motion, the algorithm and key length it uses, and who may approve an exception.

F1-3.1.name: Data at rest encryption coverage register
F1-3.1.description: Register of the places that hold classified data, such as file shares, databases, backups and endpoints, with the encryption method in use and whether each place is covered.

F1-3.1.name: Encryption exceptions register
F1-3.1.description: Register of stores of classified data that are not encrypted, with the reason, the compensating control, the approver and the date the exception expires.

F1-3.1.name: Encryption software patch status report
F1-3.1.description: Report of the version and patch level of disk, database and file encryption tools and key management systems, with the known vulnerabilities still open and the date each will be fixed.

F1-3.2.name: Laptop and desktop encryption spot checks
F1-3.2.description: Results of checks on sampled laptops and desktops showing that disk encryption is on, how the device is protected before the system starts and where the recovery key is held.

F1-3.3.name: Lost and stolen mobile device records
F1-3.3.description: Records of each lost or stolen smartphone or tablet, or a nil return for the period, showing the date it was raised, whether the device was encrypted, the lock or wipe action taken and when it was confirmed.

F1-3.4.name: Unencrypted portable media block test
F1-3.4.description: Test results showing that writing classified data to an unencrypted portable drive is blocked or forces encryption, with the date, the tester and the device used.

F1-3.5.name: Database encryption inventory
F1-3.5.description: Inventory of the databases that hold classified data, with the encryption method used, who owns the keys and whether backups and replicas are encrypted too.

F1-3.6.name: System secrets protection register
F1-3.6.description: Register of the application keys, service passwords and tokens used by systems, showing where each is held, how that store is protected and the date it was last rotated.

F1-3.6.name: Clear-text credential scan results
F1-3.6.description: Results of scans of file shares, code repositories and scripts for credentials held in clear text, with the findings and the date each was fixed.

F1-4.1.name: Approved secure transport protocols
F1-4.1.description: Document naming the protocols and versions allowed for web, file transfer, remote administration and wireless traffic that carries non-open data, and the older ones that are banned, with its owner and version.

F1-4.2.name: Mail transport encryption settings
F1-4.2.description: Mail gateway and server settings showing how encrypted transport is applied to mail exchanged with other organizations, and what happens when the receiving server cannot support it.

F1-4.2.name: Email encryption rule settings
F1-4.2.description: Settings of the rules that encrypt, or require the sender to encrypt, messages and attachments that carry non-open data, with a sample of messages that triggered them.

F1-4.3.name: Network path encryption review
F1-4.3.description: Review of the network paths that carry non-open data, such as internal segments, wireless, branch and remote links, showing which are encrypted, which rely on segmentation alone and the risk accepted for each.

F1-5.1.name: Cryptographic key inventory
F1-5.1.description: Inventory of the cryptographic keys in use, with their purpose, algorithm, key length, owner, storage location and creation and expiry dates.

F1-5.1.name: Key custodian appointments
F1-5.1.description: Signed appointments naming the people who may generate, use, back up and destroy keys, with the separation between these roles, each custodian's acceptance and, where a hardware security module is used, the administrator roles and the quorum needed for key operations.

F1-5.2.name: Key generation settings
F1-5.2.description: Settings of the hardware security module or key service that creates keys, showing the approved algorithms and key lengths, the random number source and the roles allowed to generate keys.

F1-5.2.name: Key generation ceremony record
F1-5.2.description: Record of the creation of a high-value key, such as a master or root key, showing the date, the approved tool or module used, who requested and approved it and, where a ceremony is held, who attended and the checks made.

F1-5.3.name: Key distribution and receipt records
F1-5.3.description: Records of each key or key component handed over, showing the sender, the receiver, the method used, the date and the receiver's confirmation of receipt.

F1-5.3.name: Key transport protection settings
F1-5.3.description: Settings of the key exchange and key wrapping used to send keys between systems and people, showing they travel only over protected channels and never in clear text.

F1-5.4.name: Key store access review results
F1-5.4.description: Results of the review of who can read, export or administer each key store, confirmed by the key owner, with access removed where it is no longer needed.

F1-5.5.name: Key backup and escrow arrangements
F1-5.5.description: Description of where key backups and escrowed copies are held, how they are protected, who can retrieve them and any dual control or split knowledge applied to retrieval.

F1-5.6.name: Key destruction records
F1-5.6.description: Records of keys destroyed, showing the key identifier, the reason, the method, the date due and the date done, and who carried out the destruction and, where the entity's rules ask for it, who witnessed it.

F1-5.7.name: Key archive register
F1-5.7.description: Register of keys moved to the archive, with the reason each is kept, such as reading old encrypted data, its archive location, retention period and who approved access.

F1-6.1.name: Long-term data exposure assessment
F1-6.1.description: Assessment of which non-open data must stay confidential for many years and could be copied now and decrypted later, used to set the order in which systems move to quantum-safe cryptography.

F1-6.1.name: Cryptographic agility assessment
F1-6.1.description: Assessment of whether each system can change algorithms and key sizes without being rebuilt, with the dependencies and vendor support that limit the change.

F2-2.1.name: Remote work security policy
F2-2.1.description: Approved policy for secure remote work that says who may work remotely, from where, on which devices and under which controls, with its owner, version and approval date.

F2-2.1.name: Remote work security procedures
F2-2.1.description: Step-by-step procedures for authorizing a remote worker, issuing and returning equipment, reporting a lost device and ending remote access, with the owner of each.

F2-2.1.name: National remote work conformance review
F2-2.1.description: Review of how well the entity's remote work rules, access methods and device controls meet each section of the national remote work requirements, with the shortfalls found, who owns each and when it will be closed.

F2-2.2.name: Remote work risk assessment
F2-2.2.description: Assessment of the security risks of remote work, such as unmanaged networks, lost devices and shared workspaces, with the rating, owner and treatment of each and its place in the entity's main risk register.

F2-2.2.name: Remote work risk monitoring report
F2-2.2.description: Periodic report to management on remote work risks, covering new risks, treatment progress, remote work incidents and indicators such as unmanaged devices and failed authentication attempts.

F2-2.3.name: Remote worker awareness material
F2-2.3.description: Awareness material for remote workers covering safe use of home and public networks, device handling, phishing, protecting data away from the office and how to raise an incident.

F2-2.3.name: Remote worker baseline completion report
F2-2.3.description: Report showing each remote worker completed the baseline awareness, with the completion date, and the follow-up on anyone who has not.

F2-3.1.name: Zero Trust remote access model
F2-3.1.description: Document showing how remote access applies Zero Trust: every user and device is verified on each request, access is limited to named applications, and trust is re-evaluated during the session.

F2-3.1.name: Remote device posture check settings
F2-3.1.description: Settings that check the state of a device before it reaches the entity's applications, such as whether it is managed, encrypted, patched and protected by endpoint security tools, and block or limit it if a check fails.

F2-3.1.name: Remote access session logs
F2-3.1.description: Extracts of the remote access gateway logs showing, for each session, the user, device, time, source, applications reached and result, kept for the period the entity has set.

F2-3.2.name: Remote access entitlement list
F2-3.2.description: Export of the accounts allowed to connect remotely, with the systems each can reach, the approver and the date approved.

F2-3.2.name: Remote multi-factor enforcement test
F2-3.2.description: Test showing that a remote connection attempt without the second factor is refused, for each type of user allowed to connect remotely, with the date, the tester and the systems tested.

F2-3.3.name: Remote worker onboarding checklists
F2-3.3.description: Completed checklists for sampled new remote workers showing screening, equipment issue, acceptance of the rules, induction and access approval were completed, with the dates.

F2-3.3.name: Remote worker offboarding checklists
F2-3.3.description: Completed checklists for sampled leavers showing remote access was removed, equipment was returned and work data was deleted from any personal device, with the dates.

F2-4.1.name: Off-network device compliance report
F2-4.1.description: Report showing that entity provided devices used outside the office receive updates and security tool definitions while off the corporate network, and listing those that are out of date.

F2-4.2.name: Mobile device compliance rule settings
F2-4.2.description: Settings in the mobile device management tool that block or quarantine non-compliant devices, such as those that are rooted or jailbroken, run an unsupported system version or have no screen lock.

F2-4.2.name: Approved mobile application list
F2-4.2.description: List of the applications approved for managed mobile devices, with the owner and the date approved, and the application types that are blocked.

F2-4.3.name: Signed BYOD agreements
F2-4.3.description: Agreements signed by users of personal devices accepting that the entity may apply security controls to them, such as keeping work data apart from personal data and wiping the work data if the device is lost or the user leaves.

F2-4.3.name: Third-party device access restrictions
F2-4.3.description: Settings that limit what third-party devices can reach, such as a virtual desktop or browser-only access to named applications, with downloads and local storage turned off.

F2-5.1.name: Remote work data location rules
F2-5.1.description: Rules stating in which countries, and on which systems and devices, organization data may be accessed, stored and handled during remote work, and whether working from abroad is allowed.

F2-5.1.name: Remote access country restriction settings
F2-5.1.description: Gateway or conditional access settings that block connections from countries and networks where remote work is not allowed.

F2-5.1.name: Remote work abroad approvals
F2-5.1.description: Approvals for working from outside the country, showing the worker, the country, the dates, the data allowed and the approver.

F2-5.2.name: Approved remote data transfer methods
F2-5.2.description: List of the ways remote workers may send or share organization data, such as the managed file share and encrypted email, with the classification each may carry, and the channels that are prohibited.

F2-5.2.name: Remote upload restriction settings
F2-5.2.description: Settings on remote worker devices and the access gateway that stop organization data being copied to personal storage, printed or sent through unapproved tools.

F2-5.3.name: Remote work obligations register
F2-5.3.description: Register of the obligations that apply when work is done remotely, from laws, regulations and client terms, such as data protection, confidentiality and data location, each with its owner and the control that meets it.

F3-2.1.name: National third-party security conformance review
F3-2.1.description: Review of how the entity selects, onboards and monitors suppliers against each section of the national third-party security requirements, recording where it falls short and who is responsible for each fix.

F3-2.2.name: Third-party risk awareness material
F3-2.2.description: Awareness material for staff who select, buy from or manage suppliers, covering supplier cyber security risks, how to reduce them and how to raise a supplier problem.

F3-2.2.name: Supplier-facing staff training completion report
F3-2.2.description: Report of the staff in procurement, contract management and business ownership roles who completed the supplier risk training, with follow-up on those who have not.

F3-3.1.name: Supplier criticality criteria
F3-3.1.description: Criteria used to rate how critical each supplier is, such as the data it handles, the systems it supports, how hard it is to replace and the impact if it fails.

F3-3.1.name: Supplier register completeness check
F3-3.1.description: Reconciliation of the supplier register with payment records, purchase orders and system access lists, showing no active supplier is missing and the additions made.

F3-3.2.name: Supplier classification worksheets
F3-3.2.description: Worksheets for sampled suppliers showing the inputs used, such as data handled, access held and system dependency, the tier given, the approver and the date, and any later reclassification.

F3-3.3.name: Supply chain dependency map
F3-3.3.description: Map of the entity's key suppliers and of the sub-suppliers, products and services behind them, showing the dependencies and the single points of failure.

F3-3.3.name: Third-party risk register
F3-3.3.description: Register of the cyber security risks that suppliers and their products or services bring, with the supplier concerned, the rating, the owner and the treatment status.

F3-3.4.name: Supplier risk status report
F3-3.4.description: Periodic report to management on the risk position of critical suppliers, covering changes in rating, open findings, incidents and the progress of the mitigation agreed.

F3-4.1.name: Supplier selection scoring sheet
F3-4.1.description: Scoring sheet used in tenders that weighs the security criteria next to cost and capability, with any minimum security score the entity sets and the scores of sampled bids.

F3-4.2.name: Supplier response verification records
F3-4.2.description: Records showing a supplier's answers were checked against proof, such as independent audit reports, test results or a visit, with the differences found and how they were resolved.

F3-5.1.name: Tender security requirement extracts
F3-5.1.description: Extracts of tender or purchase request documents for sampled hardware and software purchases, showing the security requirements were included and who approved them.

F3-5.2.name: Vendor product security documentation
F3-5.2.description: Security documents gathered for sampled products before purchase, such as the vendor's security statement, independent test results and the list of software components, with the evaluator's notes.

F3-5.3.name: Delivery acceptance check records
F3-5.3.description: Records of the acceptance checks made on delivered hardware and software before use, such as packaging seals, serial numbers against the order, firmware or software version, factory accounts and security tests.

F3-5.4.name: Supplier maintenance and support terms
F3-5.4.description: Extracts of the terms with suppliers for patches, upgrades and maintenance, showing the response times, the security update commitment and the conditions for remote maintenance.

F3-5.4.name: Supplier maintenance session records
F3-5.4.description: Record of each remote or on-site maintenance session by a supplier, showing who took part, when, what was done, who approved and supervised it, and when access ended.

F3-5.5.name: End-of-support register
F3-5.5.description: Register of software and hardware with the date the vendor ends support, the planned replacement or compensating control, and the owner.

F3-5.5.name: Retired hardware data erasure records
F3-5.5.description: Records showing data was erased or media destroyed when hardware was retired or returned to the supplier, with the asset, the method, the date and the person who confirmed it.

F3-5.6.name: Software component inventory
F3-5.6.description: Inventory of the open-source and third-party components used in the entity's own applications, with their versions, source and any known vulnerabilities.

F3-5.6.name: Build and release pipeline controls
F3-5.6.description: Settings of the build and release pipeline, such as builds produced from approved source only, approval needed before release and secrets kept in a protected store.

F3-6.1.name: Minimum supplier security requirements
F3-6.1.description: Document that sets the minimum security posture each supplier must meet, by supplier tier, such as access control, encryption, incident notification and audit rights.

F3-6.2.name: Supplier contract clause coverage review
F3-6.2.description: Review of the contracts with critical suppliers against the required security clauses, showing which clauses are missing and the amendment planned.

F3-6.3.name: Supplier legal compliance statements
F3-6.3.description: Statements signed by suppliers confirming they comply with the laws and regulations that apply to the service, as their obligation under the entity's terms, with any exception explained.

F3-7.1.name: Supplier performance review minutes
F3-7.1.description: Minutes of periodic meetings with critical suppliers on service levels, security findings and incidents, with the actions agreed and their owners.

F3-7.1.name: Supplier non-compliance tracker
F3-7.1.description: Tracker of supplier failures to meet the agreed security terms, with the action requested, the dates raised and closed, and any escalation.

F3-7.2.name: Supplier activity record tamper protection settings
F3-7.2.description: Settings showing the records of supplier activity are kept where the supplier cannot change or delete them, with integrity protection and the retention period.

F3-7.3.name: Enhanced controls for high-risk suppliers
F3-7.3.description: Document setting the extra controls required of suppliers rated high risk, such as more frequent checks, tighter access and on-site audits, and the schedule applied.

F3-7.3.name: High-risk supplier assurance schedule
F3-7.3.description: Schedule of the suppliers rated high risk, with the date of the last and next enhanced assessment, the findings still open and the owner.

F3-8.1.name: Supplier incident notification requirements
F3-8.1.description: Extracts of the terms and procedures that require suppliers to tell the entity about incidents within set times, naming the contact points and what must be reported.

F3-8.1.name: Supplier incident contact list
F3-8.1.description: List of the incident contacts at each critical supplier, with their roles and numbers, and the date each contact was last confirmed.

F3-8.1.name: Supplier incident response playbook
F3-8.1.description: Playbook for an incident that starts at or affects a supplier, such as a breach or an outage, with the steps, the decision makers, the messages to the supplier and the evidence to collect.

F3-8.2.name: Alternate supplier register
F3-8.2.description: Register giving, for each critical supplier, the alternate supplier or in-house fallback, the time needed to switch and the date the option was last checked.

F3-8.2.name: Supplier exit and substitution plans
F3-8.2.description: Plans for replacing a critical supplier, with the steps, the return or deletion of the entity's data, the timeline and the owner.

F3-8.3.name: Critical supplier failure impact analysis
F3-8.3.description: Analysis of the effect on each critical service if a supplier fails, with the recovery time the entity needs from that supplier.

F3-8.3.name: Supplier continuity assurance records
F3-8.3.description: Continuity plans or test summaries obtained from critical suppliers and the entity's notes on whether they meet its recovery needs.

F3-8.4.name: Supplier collaboration requirements
F3-8.4.description: Extracts of supplier terms and communications that require suppliers to join the entity's exercises and to share threat and incident information, with the contact route.

F3-8.4.name: Joint exercise report
F3-8.4.description: Report of an incident or continuity exercise held with suppliers, showing who took part, the scenario, the results and the actions agreed.

F4-2.1.name: Data exchange security policy
F4-2.1.description: Approved policy for the secure exchange of data inside the entity and with other parties, with its owner, version and approval date.

F4-2.1.name: Data exchange roles and owners
F4-2.1.description: Document naming the executive sponsor, the owner of each data exchange and the people who approve new exchanges, with their authority and the resources given.

F4-2.1.name: National data exchange conformance review
F4-2.1.description: Review of the entity's data exchange channels, controls and approvals against each section of the national data exchange requirements, with the shortfalls found, their owners and closing dates.

F4-2.2.name: Data exchange risk assessment
F4-2.2.description: Assessment of the security and privacy risks of each way data is exchanged, covering the data, the partners and the channel, with the rating, owner and treatment chosen.

F4-2.2.name: Data exchange risk treatment tracker
F4-2.2.description: Tracker of the actions that reduce data exchange risks, with the owner, the date each risk was raised and the date it was closed.

F4-2.3.name: Data exchange obligations register
F4-2.3.description: Register of the laws, regulations and sector rules that apply to exchanging data, each with its owner, the exchanges it affects and the control that meets it.

F4-2.4.name: Data exchange handling rules by classification
F4-2.4.description: Rules stating which classification levels may be exchanged, over which channels, with what approval and protection, and how exchanged files must be labeled.

F4-2.4.name: Exchange integrity protection settings
F4-2.4.description: Settings showing exchanged files and messages are protected against alteration, such as digital signatures or checksum verification, and what happens when a check fails.

F4-2.5.name: Personal data exchange register
F4-2.5.description: Register of the exchanges that include personal or sensitive personal information, with the purpose, the recipient, the legal basis and the data fields shared.

F4-2.5.name: Data minimization check results
F4-2.5.description: Results of checks on sampled exchanges showing only the personal data needed for the stated purpose is shared, with fields removed or masked where it is not.

F4-3.1.name: Data exchange authentication settings
F4-3.1.description: Settings of the data exchange services showing how users and systems authenticate, such as multi-factor authentication for people and certificates or keys for systems, with no shared or anonymous access.

F4-3.1.name: Partner and service account register
F4-3.1.description: Register of the partner and non-human accounts that connect to data exchange services, with the owner, purpose, type of credential and date it was last changed.

F4-3.2.name: Data exchange access approval records
F4-3.2.description: Sampled requests for access to data exchange services, showing the request, the data owner's approval, the access granted and the date.

F4-3.2.name: Data exchange access review results
F4-3.2.description: Extract of the completed access rights reviews covering the data exchange services, confirmed by the data owner, with the access removed or changed.

F4-3.3.name: Data exchange user activity logs
F4-3.3.description: Extracts of logs showing, for sampled transfers, who sent, received, opened or downloaded the data, from where and when.

F4-4.1.name: Data exchange channel encryption register
F4-4.1.description: Register of each data exchange mechanism, such as file transfer, application interface, messaging and portal, with the encryption protocol and version in use and the partner it serves.

F4-4.1.name: Partner connection encryption test results
F4-4.1.description: Test results showing partner connections accept only approved protocols and strengths and that connections offering weak protection are refused.

F4-5.1.name: Data exchange network redundancy diagram
F4-5.1.description: Diagram of the duplicated links, devices and providers behind the data exchange services, showing how traffic moves to the standby path on failure.

F4-5.1.name: Network failover test results
F4-5.1.description: Results of tests that moved traffic to the standby link or device, with the date, the time taken to recover and the issues found.

F4-5.2.name: Firewall rule review results
F4-5.2.description: Results of the periodic review of the rules protecting data exchange systems, showing unused or overly broad rules removed and an owner and business reason for each rule kept.

F4-5.3.name: VPN connection register
F4-5.3.description: Register of the VPN tunnels and user groups that reach data exchange systems, with the owner, the networks reachable, the encryption used and the date last checked.

F4-5.4.name: DMZ architecture diagram
F4-5.4.description: Diagram of the DMZ showing the systems placed in it and the firewall rules between the internet, the DMZ and the internal network.

F4-5.4.name: DMZ stored data check
F4-5.4.description: Check of the hosts in the DMZ for sensitive data stored on them, with the method used, the date, the findings and what was removed or protected.

F4-5.5.name: Exchange endpoint certificate inventory
F4-5.5.description: Inventory of the certificates securing the data exchange endpoints, with the issuer, expiry date, key size and owner, and the alerts set for coming expiry.

F4-5.6.name: Intrusion prevention sensor settings
F4-5.6.description: Settings of the sensors that watch data exchange traffic, showing the segments covered, whether they block or only alert, and the date signatures were last updated.

F4-5.6.name: Intrusion alert handling records
F4-5.6.description: Sample alerts raised on data exchange traffic, with how each was triaged, escalated or closed and the time taken.

F4-5.7.name: Data loss prevention rule settings
F4-5.7.description: Extract of the data leak prevention configuration showing the rules that detect and block classified or personal data leaving through email, web upload and file transfer, with the channels covered.

F4-5.7.name: Data loss prevention alert records
F4-5.7.description: Extract of the leakage monitoring and blocked transmission records: sample alerts and blocked transmissions, with how each was investigated and closed and the cases found to be false alarms.

F4-6.1.name: Data exchange system inventory
F4-6.1.description: Inventory of the systems that make up the data exchange service, such as gateways, transfer servers and message brokers, with the owner, version and security baseline applied.

F4-6.1.name: Completed hardening checklists
F4-6.1.description: Checklists completed for sampled data exchange systems showing the hardening steps were done, such as default accounts removed and unneeded services and ports closed, with the date and the person who did it.

F4-6.2.name: Data exchange configuration drift report
F4-6.2.description: Report of changes made to data exchange system configurations outside change control, with the investigation made and the fix applied.

F4-6.3.name: Data exchange penetration test report
F4-6.3.description: Report of a penetration test of the data exchange systems and their interfaces, with the date, scope, findings by severity and the status of each fix.

F4-7.1.name: Data exchange event recording coverage matrix
F4-7.1.description: Matrix of the data exchange components against the events each one records, such as authentication, transfers, system changes and errors, showing all send their event records to central storage.

F4-7.1.name: Event forwarding and retention settings
F4-7.1.description: Settings showing the event records of each data exchange component are forwarded to a central store, who can change or delete them there, and the retention period.

F4-7.2.name: Data exchange anomaly detection rules
F4-7.2.description: Settings of the rules that flag unusual exchange activity, such as large or off-hours transfers, new recipients and repeated failures.

F4-7.2.name: Inappropriate use case records
F4-7.2.description: Cases where monitoring found inappropriate access to or use of data exchange systems, with the investigation outcome, the action taken and the time taken to remediate.
